tob-10233: The Dhammapada gathers 423 short verses that sum up the Buddha’s core teachings in memorable form. Each saying addresses the mind, craving, anger, or kindness — the everyday forces that shape a person’s life. Max Müller’s translation is one of the classic English versions. For many readers, this slim collection is the most direct doorway into Buddhism.
tob-13333: Frazer’s Golden Bough — here in one-volume shape — roams the world’s myths to trace how wonder-working ripened into worship. Nemi’s priest, the corn-spirit, the scapegoat: his witnesses built a new lore of matched beliefs. On letters alone the book’s sway was huge.
tob-4214-10833: This volume of Schopenhauer’s essays takes on faith — a keen dialogue holding religion a needful tale for the many, with pieces on right-doing and first things. His godlessness braces like his gloom. Saunders’s English keeps the old lion’s roar.
tob-0033: This 1955 Air Force report is the weightiest official UFO study ever printed — a numbers-crunching of 3,201 sightings by the Battelle Memorial Institute. Its finding: no proof of star-ships, but a hard core of cases none could crack. The report stays the bedrock of sober saucer research.
tob-0133: The Gheranda Samhita ranks among the three great books of hatha yoga — a talk in which the sage Gheranda schools a king in the sevenfold road of body-cleansing. Its verses spell out postures, seals, and breath-holdings in full. The work mates the Hatha Yoga Pradipika.
tob-4333: Watts’s Englishing of St. Augustine’s Shrift — book two — bears on with the great soul-tale, the saint’s fare from sin to sainthood. His rendering made Augustine’s heart-speech speak our tongue. The Shrift stays the ground-text of western self-baring, the most aped soul-tale ever penned.
tob-10033: Frazer’s Englishing of Ovid’s Year-Book gives the Roman month-roll in verse — wonder-tales and rites for every month. The poem is our fullest well for Roman high-days. Only six months live on; the rest was never finished. This printing bears Ovid’s learning and wit to English readers.
tob-10333: The Malleus Maleficarum — the Hammer of Witches, 1486 — is the infamous inquisitors’ manual by Kramer and Sprenger. Its lurid demonology taught how to hunt, try, and burn witches. The book fueled two centuries of persecution. It stands as the darkest monument of medieval superstition.
cia-0000112333: Take 8 of many — a March 1990 report on Gorbachev's visit to the Ural Mountains region. Soviet leaders toured the industrial heartland to rally support as the union unraveled. Numbered takes like this one suggest a series of dispatches, each capturing one stop on a leader's increasingly desperate roadshow.
cia-0000112833: An untitled October 1945 statement by S. Toropovsky. Statements from detainees and witnesses were the building blocks of postwar investigations. The entry preserves one voice from the great sorting-out of 1945 — though the archive withholds what that voice said.
cia-0000124333: An April 1959 report, its title mangled, on newspaper readers' responses to students' pleas to free American prisoners held by China. Public campaigns kept the POW issue alive years after the war. The document shows the home front refusing to forget — and the press amplifying the call.
cia-0000132633: A June 1960 report: Chinese communists concluding a trade post with Cuba — the archive's phrasing suggests a trade pact. Beijing was buying into the revolution. The document is the deal: the trade, concluded.

a-popular-history-of-ireland-from-the-ea: McGee's passionate history of Ireland appears here in another edition, carrying readers from legendary beginnings to the triumph of Catholic Emancipation. Written by an Irish nationalist who lived the cause, the narrative blends scholarship with love of country. It remains one of the most readable popular histories of the Irish people.
arxiv-2605-08733: In reinforcement learning, an actor chooses actions while a critic judges them, and Shunpu Tang, Yafei Wang, and Lisheng Fan rebuild that partnership around generative models. Their 2026 paper introduces soft bridge policies — flexible links connecting the generative actor to its critic during training. The contribution is the framework itself: a new way to structure actor-critic learning when both sides are generative.
arxiv-2605-08833: Time-series data — stock ticks, sensor streams — needs models with a memory of the past, and state space models are the current favorite. Mengqi Li, Wensheng Lin, Jinshuai Yang, and Lixin Li propose FRACTAL, a state space model with a fractional recurrent architecture for temporal analysis. The 2026 paper rethinks recurrence with fractional-order dynamics.
arxiv-2605-09233: Complex image edits happen in steps — remove this, recolor that — and each step must survive the next. Zilai Zeng, Mingdeng Cao, Zijie Li, and colleagues work toward robust sequential decomposition for image editing. The 2026 paper is about edits that do not fall apart mid-sequence.
arxiv-2605-09333: The E8 lattice is the most symmetric packing in eight dimensions, and the Okubo algebra is an exotic cousin of the octonions. Daniele Corradetti studies integral elements of the Okubo algebra and their link to E8. The 2026 paper is pure algebra on exceptional structures.
arxiv-2605-09633: Robot teams patrolling forever must minimize the worst-case wait between visits to any location. Weizhen Wang, Ziheng Wang, and colleagues tackle the problem with theory and RL-based solutions. The 2026 paper is persistent multi-robot monitoring with real guarantees.
arxiv-2605-09733: Massive, compact, quiescent galaxies in the nearby universe hide a surprisingly three-component structure. Katia Slodkowski Clerici, Allan Schnorr-Muller, and colleagues dissect them in this first installment of the series. The 2026 paper is detailed galaxy anatomy — small and complex.
arxiv-2605-09833: Compressing data across domains — accepting some loss — via constrained minimum entropy coupling is the challenge. Nam Nguyen, Thinh Nguyen, Bella Bose, and colleagues develop the cross-domain compression method. The 2026 paper is information theory for lossy, cross-domain compression theory.
arxiv-2605-10033: Orbital and spin Nernst effects — transverse currents driven by heat — in monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides. Saikat Saha, Arnab Bose, and Sayantika Bhowal investigate. The 2026 paper is 2D materials physics with a thermal twist. It finds Nernst effects in atom-thin layers.
plos-pone-0003433: Public-health modelers measured a hidden cost of the oral polio vaccine in this 2008 paper. In rare cases the weakened vaccine virus can mutate back toward virulence and spread, a risk called vaccine-derived poliovirus. The team estimated how much such infection was circulating, informing the endgame strategy for wiping out polio without the vaccine itself seeding outbreaks.
plos-pone-0003533: Geneticists found evolution's fingerprints near a prostate-cancer hotspot in this 2008 paper. A susceptibility locus inside the FHIT gene region showed a strong signature of natural selection, suggesting the same DNA stretch has been under evolutionary pressure. The finding ties cancer risk to the deeper history written in our genes.
plos-pone-0003633: Rheumatologists Dehlin, Bokarewa, and Rottapel fingered a joint-local driver of arthritis in this 2008 paper. Expression of Flt3 ligand inside arthritic joints propelled both the start and the worsening of rheumatoid inflammation. The intra-articular signal emerges as a target for calming the synovial storm at its source.
plos-pone-0003733: In 2008, Jörg Fröbisch surveyed survivors of Earth's worst extinction. Anomodonts, the plant-eating mammal relatives that weathered the end-Permian crisis 252 million years ago, were mapped for global diversity against the rock record. The diversity curves show who made it through the Great Dying and where.
plos-pone-0003833: In 2008, Seitsonen, Onkamo, and Peng studied gene teamwork in blinding eye disease. Variants in complement factor H and the LOC387715 region showed combined effects on age-related macular degeneration risk. The interaction data refine who faces the highest odds of losing central vision.
plos-pone-0003933: In 2008, Jin, Lv, and Chen built a bird-flu vaccine on a silkworm system. Their H5N1 vaccine used baculovirus surface display in Bombyx mori to present viral proteins. Tests showed the shot was safe and triggered immune responses. The silkworm platform offers a fast, scalable route to pandemic vaccines.
plos-pone-0004033: In 2008, Grieve, Dickens, and Pravenec mapped gene teamwork across the body. Their genome-wide co-expression analysis spanned multiple human and animal tissue types. The team also folded in expression quantitative trait loci, or eQTLs. The multi-tissue map shows where gene partnerships hold and where they shift.
plos-pone-0004133: In 2009, Wang, Ziman, and Bodi watched mouse hearts fail in stages. Mice overproducing a calcium channel pore first turned hypercontractile. Then diastolic trouble and dilated cardiomyopathy followed. The staged collapse maps heart failure's arc. The sequence gives drug hunters stage-specific targets.
plos-pone-0004233: In 2009, a French team found hepatitis C hitching a ride. The virus's coat release depended on the liver's fat-shipping assembly line. The germ piggybacked on the fat transport system cleverly. The dependence exposes a host target for new drug designs.
plos-pone-0004333: In 2009, Arking, Khera, and Xing found key heart-rhythm genes. Multiple independent genetic factors at NOS1AP tuned the heart's QT interval across ethnicities. The heart's fine electrical timing had several separate genetic dials. The neat finding refines sudden-death risk prediction models.
plos-pone-0358433: Drones wobble in wind — and precise flight needs control that fights back. This paper designed trajectory tracking control for UAVs using a disturbance observer with robust adaptive neural dynamic surface. The controller keeps the drone on path even as gusts and model errors push it off.
plos-pone-0358233: Ranking Kyoto’s streets from incomplete pairwise comparisons is a puzzle with missing pieces. This paper compared ranking methods on intersection names to street rankings with incomplete data. The bake-off shows which algorithms handle patchy, partial preferences best — useful far beyond one Japanese city.
plos-pone-0342133: Eye clinics are overwhelmed — could asynchronous review relieve the pressure? This discrete choice experiment measured preferences for community-based asynchronous-review eye clinics among UK patients, healthcare professionals, and the public. The preferences reveal whether people will accept quality eye care without the face-to-face appointment.
plos-pone-0357633: Stigma in healthcare is a structural problem demanding structural solutions, not just kinder attitudes. This qualitative study examined stigma reduction as quality health care, focusing on structural-level mechanisms that address it. The identified mechanisms show institutions concretely how to change.
plos-pone-0348533: Tiny objects in images defeat most detectors — especially when a single sensor type can’t see them clearly. This research developed multimodal dense small object detection algorithms guided by cross-modal information. The fusion approach finds what any single sensor would miss.
plos-pone-0357733: Kurort health walking — therapeutic strolls rooted in Japan’s spa tradition — blends nature with exercise. This before-after study measured the physiological and psychological outcomes of a community-based program. The results show walking in healing landscapes restores both body and mind.
plos-pone-0357033: Anemic mothers giving birth at mid-altitudes face compounded risks that lowland protocols miss. This paper presents maternal outcomes at mid-altitudes in anemic pregnant women, drawing on evidence from the WOMAN-2 trial. The findings guide safer maternal care for mountain communities.
plos-pone-0354633: Hospitalized patients sleep terribly — and improving it starts with measuring it well. This cross-sectional validation study tested the Verran and Snyder-Halpern sleep scale and a sleep-influences questionnaire in Dutch hospitals. The validated tools give wards a reliable way to track — and improve — patient sleep.
plos-pone-0357233: The brain’s cerebrospinal fluid factory — the choroid plexus — ages in ways we barely understand. This paper studied age-related molecular and functional remodeling of the choroid plexus in the gray mouse lemur, a small primate. The findings illuminate how brain aging unfolds at the blood-brain barrier.
plos-pone-0355933: ‘Lose the label’ — messaging that humanizes people with criminal records can shift political perceptions. This study tested messaging effects on Democrats’ perceptions of formerly incarcerated individuals and their political representation. The findings give reform campaigns evidence-based communication tools.
plos-pone-0355833: Long-acting HIV PrEP could breed drug resistance through evolution’s own logic. This paper built a Darwinian model for the evolution of drug resistance to long-acting PrEP during early HIV infection. The evolutionary modeling warns where resistance will emerge — and how to forestall it.
plos-pone-0336733: Plants remember heat — and two distantly related wild crucifers remember it similarly. This paper found conserved gene- and network-level thermal memory intervals in two divergent perennial crucifers growing in nature. The shared molecular memory suggests deep evolutionary roots for heat preparedness — knowledge that could help breed crops for a hotter world.
plos-pone-0356533: Periostin — a protein involved in tissue repair — may mark heart attacks even after death. This paper measured serum periostin levels in myocardial infarction using forensic autopsy cases. The postmortem findings could give forensic pathologists a molecular witness when the heart can no longer speak.
plos-pone-0356233: RSV immunization products are new — and pediatricians’ attitudes will decide their uptake. This multi-country cross-sectional survey measured pediatricians’ attitudes and knowledge. The findings reveal where education must go so that infant RSV protection reaches every eligible child.
plos-pone-0355733: Screening mood rapidly — in Thai — requires a validated instrument. This paper tested the reliability and validity of the Thai Rapid Mood Screener (RMS-T). The validated screener brings quick, trustworthy mood assessment to Thai-speaking patients who need it.
europmc-pmc2820433: Evolutionary trees are hard to work with by hand, so these 2010 authors built a Python toolkit for them. ETE, the Environment for Tree Exploration, lets biologists manipulate, annotate, and visualize phylogenetic trees in code. The paper introduces the package and its design. It became a widely used library for tree-based analysis in bioinformatics.
europmc-pmc2851733: HIV may wound the gut wall itself, this 2010 lab study warns. The team shows the virus cracks the gut lining's seal, letting germ bits leak into blood. Their dish tests bare the breach. The breach helps tell why HIV sparks body-wide inflammation.
europmc-pmc2869233: The immune signal interleukin 12 steers the body's defenses, and this 2010 review covers its infection-fighting roles. The authors survey IL-12 as a key immune regulator in infection settings. Their overview backs its therapeutic promise. The review gathered a scattered field into focus.
europmc-pmc2871133: Berry compounds get credit for heart perks, and this 2010 review checks the receipts. The authors survey current proof on flavanols and anthocyanins in cardiovascular health. Their weighing finds real but modest gains. The review gives berry fans an honest scorecard.
europmc-pmc2907333: Cancer cells that regain a gripping protein may turn less vicious. This 2010 paper shows breast carcinoma cells re-express E-cadherin during a reverting transition. The authors catch the change in the act. Their work hints at forcing tumors backward.
europmc-pmc2936333: Tiny engineered particles can harm cells, but not all in the same way. This 2010 paper shows particle harm hinges on makeup, size, and the cell type hit. The authors' three-way matrix guides safer design. Their work underpins nano-safety rules for new materials.
europmc-pmc2944833: A new way to jam a cancer-linked enzyme emerged from its crystal structure. This 2010 paper reports the crystal structure of human AKT1 with an allosteric inhibitor, revealing a new mode of kinase inhibition. The authors' snapshot guides drug design. Their find opened a fresh attack route.
europmc-pmc3001433: Heart scans got faster and easier to hold. This 2010 paper brings ShMOLLI, a heart-mapping scan done in one short breath-hold. The authors' method speeds cardiac MRI visits. Their technique spread through heart clinics. Patients hold their breath for nine beats.
europmc-pmc3008733: Sugar pills work even when patients know the truth. This 2010 trial gives open-label dummy pills for irritable bowel and finds they help. The authors' honest trial stunned doctors. Their work reframed the placebo effect. Ritual and care seem to heal on their own.
europmc-pmc3033533: Head and neck radiation can spare the saliva glands. This 2011 trial pits gland-sparing intensity-modulated radiation against the standard kind. The authors' phase 3 test favors the precise beam. Their work cut dry-mouth misery. Patients could swallow and taste again.
europmc-pmc3056833: Chinese melanoma got its profile. This 2011 study details melanoma's face in 522 Chinese patients. The authors reveal distinct patterns. Their work guides Asian skin doctors. Sole and nail melanomas dominate the cases. Sunburn plays a smaller role here. Doctors now check feet and nails first.
europmc-pmc6601033: Seeing a drug target's 3D shape lets chemists design molecules to fit it like keys in locks. This review lays out the structure-based discovery playbook: from genome data to protein structures to lead compounds. The approach promises faster, cheaper drug hunting than blind screening of chemical libraries.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-33: This 2007 GAO report looks at the SEC's watch over self-run trade groups — the stock exchanges and broker clubs that police their own members. GAO found holes in how the SEC kept tabs on these groups and urged fixes. The report pulls back the curtain on an odd setup: an industry that grades itself while a federal agency grades the graders.
gao-gaoreports-b-299533: Battelle Memorial Institute took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The research giant said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the claims against bid law. Even nonprofit research powerhouses must play by the bidding rules.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-733: The Pentagon's business computers were slowly getting governors in 2007 — GAO's report says corporate-style controls were finally taking hold. The findings credit the progress while noting the distance left. The report's hope: run the back office like a business, and the waste will shrink.
gao-gaoreports-b-299433: Weidlinger Associates doubled its May 2007 protest — two case numbers, one engineering fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims for good. The firm challenged the awards as unfair; the call weighs each claim. Engineering bid wars get the full technical hearing.
openalex-w7206178233: Democratic school management sounds good on paper; this study asks how to make it real. Reviewing books, articles, and dissertations on the topic, the authors examine how participatory planning, where teachers, families, and staff help set a school's direction, can strengthen democratic governance in public schools. It is a literature-based analysis aimed at educators who want decision-making to be shared rather than handed down from above.
openalex-w7169810833: Neutrons make amazingly fine magnetic sensors. This lab paper builds a way to read tricky wobbling magnetic fields by watching neutron waves overlap and cancel. The authors work out the math that turns wave patterns into field maps. Ultra-precise measuring at the quantum scale.
pmc-13475233: A 2026 validation study finding that PREDICT version 3.1, a widely used breast cancer survival calculator, overestimates survival in older women. Tested against population data, the tool ran optimistic for this group. The result is a caution: prediction models need checking in the exact patients they're used on.
pmc-13439333: This 2026 case series from a tropical emergency department documents a surge of melioidosis — a serious bacterial infection — after an extraordinary wet season. Heavy rains stir up the soil bacterium that causes it. The retrospective series is a warning about climate-linked infectious disease.
pmc-13433833: In this 2026 cancer paper, a CRISPR screen — systematically knocking out genes — revealed the pathways and factors that drive resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors in liver cancer. Knowing the resistance routes in advance lets doctors plan combinations. The screen turns a clinical frustration into a target list.
pmc-13351933: This 2026 review surveys the applications and limitations of AI tools in enzyme design — where machine learning succeeds and where it still stumbles. Enzyme design is a flagship test of AI in biology. The balanced assessment is useful for both optimists and skeptics.
pmc-13332333: A 2026 study exploring whether integrating dietitians into primary care dental services for children is acceptable to families and staff. Teeth and diet are obviously linked, yet the professions rarely meet. The acceptability study tests the idea's real-world fit.
pmc-13525133: This 2026 study looked beyond COVID-19 at the behavioral drivers of pandemic prevention in Ghana's informal urban settlements. Crowded settlements face unique prevention challenges. The behavioral insights inform future outbreak response.
pmc-13439933: In this 2026 C. elegans paper, researchers showed that the lipid-binding PX domain of RRC-1 is required for proper assembly and function of integrin adhesion complexes at muscle cell boundaries. The membrane-binding module anchors the adhesion machinery. The finding details how muscles grip their surroundings.
pmc-13525833: This 2026 dermatology education paper found that resident basic exam scores correlated with American Board of Dermatology certification outcomes under the new model. Early scores predict board success. The correlation validates the basic exam's role.
pmc-13470333: A 2026 review of current status and targeted therapies in endometrial cancer — molecular classification-driven treatment strategies. Molecular subtypes now guide therapy. The review organizes the new paradigm.
pmc-13465233: In this 2026 Alzheimer's paper, extracellular Aβ42 oligomers induced ROCK2 hyperactivation through dual mediation by RhoA and granzyme B — with moderate ROCK2 activity significant for neural cells (the title is truncated). The signaling cascade is a drug target. The mechanism is the finding.
pmc-13465533: A 2026 ophthalmology paper on contrast sensitivity impairment in diabetic retinopathy — clinical and structural correlates. Contrast loss precedes vision loss. The correlates guide monitoring.
pmc-13602033: A 2026 data paper presenting CaDENCE — a large-scale call disconnection event dataset from consumer Android devices. Dropped calls were logged at scale. The dataset serves network research.
pmc-13530633: This 2026 conference paper studied return to play and performance after shoulder labral repair in Major League Baseball players. The elite athletes' outcomes were tracked. The paper quantifies the comeback.
pmc-13448333: A 2026 conference abstract (TLSB-22) on tumor-associated macrophages and TNFR2 driving progression from progenitor to terminal exhaustion within the intracranial tumor microenvironment. The immune exhaustion pathway was mapped. The abstract presents the mechanism.
pmc-13529133: A 2026 ophthalmology case report of late traumatic LASIK flap perforation and displacement by a bird bite. The bizarre injury is the hook. The case documents the repair.
pmc-13518033: A 2026 emergency medicine case report: tension hydrocele — how point-of-care ultrasound helped in the ED. The bedside scan solved the scrotal emergency. The case teaches the technique.
pmc-13480233: A 2026 cardiology paper: "Eisenmenger Syndrome Enters the Sotatercept Era." The pulmonary hypertension drug's arrival changed the Eisenmenger landscape. The paper marks the transition.
pmc-13454733: A 2026 paper engaging teenage grassroots soccer players in sports-related concussion education. The young athletes learned about head injury. The engagement is the strategy.
pmc-13422133: A 2026 Brazilian study investigating PDCD1 gene polymorphisms and haplotypes in COVID-19 severity and outcome. The immune checkpoint gene's variants were tested. The investigation is the genetics.
pmc-13487433: A 2026 phylogenomics paper: mitoplastomic discordance in Brassicaceae confirmed the complex evolutionary history of the mustard family. The conflicting genomes told a tangled story. The discordance is the evidence.
pmc-13510033: In this 2026 Sudanese study, vitamin D deficiency was examined as a potential modifier of hematological outcomes and vaso-occlusive crisis frequency in sickle cell disease (the title is truncated). The vitamin's modifying role was tested. The evidence is the data.
pmc-13430933: A 2026 retraction notice for a paper on physicochemical, antioxidant, organoleptic, and anti-diabetic properties of beef burgers enriched with fruit juices (the title is truncated). The paper was withdrawn. The retraction amends the record.
pmc-13472933: A 2026 lung cancer paper: ctDNA-derived copy-number signatures associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance beyond PD-L1 and TMB in advanced NSCLC. The blood-based resistance markers were found. The signatures are the predictive advance.
pmc-13427233: A 2026 mechanics paper: bistable networks enabled complex shape changes. The snap-through structures morphed. The enabling is the materials advance.
pmc-13524133: In this 2026 paper, dynamic discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimated glomerular filtration rates was examined across forniceal rupture and its surgical decompression (the title is truncated). The kidney markers disagreed dynamically. The discordance informs nephrology.
pmc-13468133: This 2026 physics paper reported the piezochiral effect. The new electromechanical phenomenon was discovered. The effect is the physics.
pmc-13419233: In this 2026 paper, the long horizon of animal study preregistration was examined — attitudes, barriers, and myths. The preregistration culture was surveyed. The examining serves research integrity.
arxiv-2606-16433: Protons kicked into their excited cousin, the Delta baryon, reveal the proton's inner structure. This nuclear-physics paper computes the chiral-odd tensor form factors of that N-to-Delta transition using QCD light-cone sum rules. It targets hadron physicists mapping how quarks and gluons arrange themselves inside matter.
arxiv-2606-16833: OMC-2 FIR4 is a clump of gas and dust birthing stars in Orion. This paper hunts oxygen there — a key ingredient of water and life's chemistry — using telescope observations. It is for astrochemists mapping the raw materials of brand-new planets.
